title: automated-artifact-pipeline-for-open-llm-onboarding
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Scope: Build an end-to-end automated pipeline that ingests open-source LLM weight artifacts, converts/normalizes formats (safetensors, PyTorch .pt, Hugging Face sharded checkpoints), runs conversion and lightweight quantization passes, executes validation and acceptance tests, and publishes a pinned model artifact with a canonical performance profile into the model catalog. The pipeline must emit a manifest.json, cryptographic checksums, semantic version tags, and an immutable artifact URL that can be referenced by Redwood runtime and Dedicated clusters.

Goals:
- Reliable weights intake with artifact provenance and license verification.
- Deterministic conversion with reproducible checksums and deterministic shard ordering.
- Validation suite covering unit inference checks, KV cache key compatibility, tokenizer parity, and small-batch performance smoke tests.
- Perf profiling across target hardware configurations (V100/A10/H100) and sequence lengths (256/1024/4096) to capture latency P50/P95 and token throughput.
- Automatic publish of model-card + performance profile to model-catalog with pinned-version metadata and fallback variants (quantized/int8/fp16).

Non-goals: full-scale long-horizon evals (these are handled by the research evals pipeline), model licensing disputes (alert and block; legal team handles).
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests .safetensors and multi-shard HF checkpoints and stores canonical artifact under artifacts.redwood.ai with SHA256 checksum
Conversion step produces model artifact that passes the conversion smoke tests on CPU and GPU runtimes
Automated validation runs: tokenizer roundtrip, sample inference output match within tolerance, KV cache restore test
Perf profile job executes on target fleet, outputs P50/P95 latencies and tokens/sec for 256/1024/4096 sequences
Model catalog entry created with pinned semantic version (e.g., m-XXX@v1.0.0), manifest, license, and performance profile visible in Console
Manifest schema v2.0 emitted and validated by CI; immutability enforced (artifacts immutable once published)
Alerting on validation failures with clear triage steps and automatic rollback of partial publishes

2025-01-22 - Design review (K. Rivera): Model card template approved; include license, intended-use, known-failure modes, and responsible-owner fields.
2025-01-28 - CI: Added conversion pipeline job in Jenkins 'models-convert' that runs on an ephemeral GPU pool. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/587
2025-01-30 - Performance team: Profiling harness integrated with perf-runner. First run on A10 shows P95 ~ 420ms for 1024 tokens; need to add KV cache warmup to measurement harness.
2025-02-03 - Markus Chen: Blocker discovered - some HF checkpoints use legacy config keys that break tokenizer mapping. Workaround added: config-mapper v0.2; follow-up cleanup in converter.
2025-02-05 - Legal (S. Park): Automated license scanner added; pipeline will mark artifacts requiring manual review and block publish for non-permissive licenses.
2025-02-07 - QA: Validation suite results for m-llama-prototype-8b attached to ticket; two failing downstream ops tests (KV restore flaky). Investigating race in cache restore code path.
notes: Implementation notes: prefer safetensors as canonical published format to avoid pickling risks. Use semantic versioning where major bump indicates ABI-incompatible tokenizer or tensor layout changes. Publish performance profile artifacts as separate JSON blobs and attach badges (green/yellow/red) to model catalog based on acceptance thresholds. Ensure conversion jobs run in isolated ephemeral infra with IAM-scoped service accounts. Generate a small 'canary' pinned model used for smoke rollouts before assigning to Dedicated pools.
